title: Tenant-aware audit shaping and adaptive delivery for SIEM/webhook sinks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a tenant-aware audit delivery stack that negotiates delivery contracts per external sink (SIEM/Datadog/Splunk/webhook), enforces tenant-level shaping to avoid noisy-tenant storms, and provides strong delivery semantics with observable failure modes. This ticket covers design, API contracts, and an initial implementation for webhook/SIEM connectors and the adaptive forwarding layer.

Background: Current audit forwarder sends a single undifferentiated stream to external sinks which has led to capacity and quota failures for high-volume tenants. On top of that, external SIEMs have heterogeneous expectations (some require batched payloads, some prefer streaming webhooks, some have strict rate-limits). We need a system that: 1) negotiates or encodes a sink contract, 2) enforces tenant shaping and backpressure so one tenant cannot impact others, 3) provides clear at-least-once semantics with idempotency and deduplication options, and 4) surfaces intelligible telemetry and runbook actions.

Scope:
- Contract negotiation model for each sink type (webhook, Splunk HEC, Datadog intake). Contract includes preferred batch window, max requests/sec, max events/batch, recommended backoff policy, and idempotency support flag.
- Tenant shaping layer that enforces per-tenant token bucket policies and global pool limits. Configurable per-customer tags for burst behavior.
- Delivery semantics: primary goal is at-least-once with strong deduplication support via globally unique event IDs and optional exactly-once-by-ack semantics when sink supports persistent ACKs.
- Adaptive batching: dynamic batch sizing that uses sink contract, observed latencies, and queue depth to pick batch size and flush intervals.
- Failure modes and DLQ strategy: exponential backoff with jitter, per-tenant DLQ with tombstone events for auditability, and a reconciler job that surfaces missing sequences.
- Observability: per-tenant and per-sink metrics (ingest rate, egress rate, acks, retries, DLQ counts), traceable envelopes with delivery lifecycle events, and a console dashboard for tenant throttling events.

Non-goals: full migration of existing SIEM partners in this ticket; this is an incremental rollout, starting with webhooks and Splunk HEC. Deep protocol adapters for each commercial SIEM will be follow-ups.

Design decisions and trade-offs considered:
- Exactly-once vs at-least-once: Exactly-once requires coordination with the sink (idempotent write tokens or persistent ACKs) and stateful replay. We will default to at-least-once and provide opt-in exactly-once mode for partners that support it. This reduces complexity and improves availability.
- Centralized vs distributed shaping: a centralized token bucket simplifies global picture but introduces a single point of contention. We will implement tenant shaping in the forwarding plane with lightweight coordination via leases to avoid tight coupling.
- Deduplication strategy: use a 128-bit event uuid combined with per-sink sequence numbers when available. Keep dedupe windows configurable per sink to control memory.

Deliverables:
- API for sink contracts and a schema for contract negotiation (stored in tenant config).
- Forwarder changes: tenant-aware queues, adaptive batcher, and acks/retry state machine.
- Observability: metrics + tracing + dashboard prototype.
- Runbook: steps for triaging tenant-induced backpressure and steps to throttle/unthrottle.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Audit+Adaptive+Delivery+Design
- Spike notes and kernel-level perf numbers: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/0A_spike_audit_forwarder
- Initial PR (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4121

Migration plan (high level):
1) Implement off-path contract store + per-tenant shaping toggles.
2) Route a subset (~10%) of low-volume tenants through new forwarder for testing.
3) Gradually onboard a few trusted SIEM partners and enable enhanced ack path for them.
4) Measure and iterate on dedupe window and batch heuristics.

Acceptance criteria:
- New forwarder can route audit events for a tenant through an external webhook with per-tenant rate shaping enforced.
- Adaptive batching reduces API calls to partners by >30% for batched sinks without increasing median latency by more than 150ms for 99th percentile flows.
- Observability dashboard shows per-tenant throttles and DLQ counts, and the runbook successfully recovers a simulated tenant storm in staging.
- Security review completed and config flags for enabling exact-once are gated behind enterprise contracts.
acceptance_criteria: Tenant-level rate limits and burst controls are configurable and enforced in staging
Forwarder implements deduplication via event UUIDs and exposes dedupe window config
Adaptive batching algorithm exists and is testable via traffic generator with documented parameters
DLQ and reconciler surface missing sequence ranges in console and postmortem exports
Security review sign-off and audit of key storage for idempotency tokens
comments: 2025-02-13 - Marco Ruiz: Spike complete. Implemented a prototype token-bucket per tenant and a simple batcher. Measured a 42% reduction in outgoing HTTP calls when batching at 250ms vs immediate flush. Draft PR opened at https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4121

2025-02-18 - Priya Menon (SRE): Observed increased memory usage when dedupe window > 24h. Recommend starting with 1h default and exposing knob. Added dependency to ENG-59421 for sequenced ack resume behavior.

2025-02-21 - Aisha Patel (Security): Flagged that idempotency keys must be stored in a KMS-backed store if used for exactly-once. Security review required before enabling opt-in exactly-once for customers. See security checklist in Confluence.

2025-02-25 - Marco Ruiz: Implemented per-sink contract schema. Webhook contract supports max_requests_per_minute, max_batch_size, supports_idempotency boolean, preferred_content_type. Stored in tenant config service. Draft PR updated.

2025-02-28 - Design review (PM + Design): PM Sarah Kim approved contract shape; Design suggested adding backpressure reason tags for the console to highlight cause (quota vs downstream timeout). Will add a 'throttle_reason' dimension to metrics.

2025-03-03 - Marco Ruiz: Started integration test harness that simulates Splunk HEC with intermittent auth failures to validate retry/backoff policy. Initial results show successful recovery after three retries with exponential backoff and jitter. Adding DLQ tombstone write and reconciler job in next PR.

2025-03-05 - Aisha Patel (Security): Preliminary security review meeting scheduled. Need to verify that tenant shaping config cannot be modified by tenant admins unless RBAC v2 role permits. Added dependency on RBAC workstream.
2025-03-05 - Release/Next steps: Rollout plan approved to test with 10% of low-traffic tenants in staging, then 5 trusted customers in a canary. Point-of-contact: Marco Ruiz and Priya Menon.
